newsitem.title: FRANCE: Volvo sees higher U.S. car sales in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Volvo sees higher U.S. car sales in 1997.

text.p: Swedish automotive group Volvo said Wednesday it expected its car division to post higher sales in the United States next year despite a weakening of the total car market in the region.

"We expect to increase sales in the United States slightly next year. However, we see a continued weakening of the market for passenger cars, whilst the truck (sporting/utility and light truck) segment will remain strong," Volvo spokesman Fred Hammond told Reuters at the Paris car show.

Hammond said he expected a price war to break out on the car market next year. Toyota will try to boost its Camry model in the U.S. market via low prices, while Ford will respond to maintain the leading position of its Taurus, he said.
"In other words, it'll be a good year for the consumers," Hammond said.
He said Volvo Cars of North America was pleased with its sales figures so far this year, which showed a minimal downturn of less than one percent.

"We are very encouraged by the figures so far this year, and expect to reach our goal of selling as many cars this year as in 1995. You also have to remember that we are not selling the 940 model in the States this year," Hammond said, adding that the 940 had accounted for 15 percent of 1995 sales.
Volvo expects to sell around 3,000 of its new C70 model next year, but Hammond declined to predict the rest of the product mix.
